_about: Ground truth for Day 12 matching accuracy. THESE LABELS ARE JUDGMENTS MADE BY CLAUDE (an AI), NOT BY A HUMAN RECRUITER. They were written after reading each resume's extracted text and each job's profile, and BEFORE running the matcher on them. Please review them; every row with doubtful=true is a close call.

label_scale.relevant: A recruiter would shortlist this person: most must-have skills and the right kind of work.
label_scale.partly relevant: Worth a look but with clear gaps: some must-have skills or a nearby role, or a seniority mismatch.
label_scale.not relevant: Wrong field or almost no overlap with the must-have skills.

error_notes.sample_simple.pdf|jd_senior_python_messy: The resume is 132 characters: only Python of the 12 must-have skills is present and the experience line ('Intern at Demo Corp') shares no words with the job, so experience scores 0. The matcher sees too little text. It is a thin resume, and my 'partly relevant' label is a judgment about the skills, not about the text.
error_notes.Maya.pdf|jd_hr_executive: Only one skill is shared: 'crm' (she integrated CRM tools as an engineer). One of the four must-have skills gives a skills score of 15, which is just enough to reach the fold cut-off of 13. The skill overlap is real but the role overlap is not.
